report.body:
Mossos d'Esquadra officers of the Criminal Investigation Division (DIC) detained
seven men aged 29 to 55 on 1 October 2026 in an industrial warehouse in Cabanes,
Girona, allegedly linked to a drug-trafficking organisation. The detentions
followed an investigation by the DIC drug unit in Sant Feliu de Llobregat that
had identified the warehouse as used only for storing and distributing narcotic
substances. The investigation had begun in June 2026 after Mossos
intercepted a van in Viladecans, Barcelona, carrying about 2,400 kg of hashish.

During surveillance in early October officers detected repeated movements of
people and vans and the arrival of an articulated lorry. Officers watched
people replace vehicles' original registration plates with other plates fastened
by cable ties, allegedly to hinder identification. With the support of ARRO
agents from Girona officers entered the warehouse and found seven people
unloading the lorry trailer's pallets to load the hashish into different vans
for later distribution. Inspection showed the pallets held hashish hidden
among merchandise inside large raffia sacks filled with shredded rubber to
hinder detection in police or customs checks. During the search officers
found a firearm in one of the detainees' vans. Mossos valued the seized
substance at more than 16.2 million euros on the illicit market.

The seven detainees were handed to the Civil and Instruction Court (Sección
Civil y de Instrucción) in Figueres. The Catalan interior minister Núria
Parlon used the Mossos information to renew calls for higher prison sentences
for large-scale cannabis trafficking.

report.summary: A judge ordered pre-trial detention for the truck driver arrested by UDYCO at the port of Ceuta after bags of hashish were found hidden in his vehicle. Police said the investigation continues, with the official weighing still pending and other outlets estimating about 300 kilograms.
report.body:
Spain's UDYCO drug unit arrested a truck driver at the port of Ceuta carrying a
stash of hashish hidden in a sophisticated false bottom. Officers
intercepted the truck on the port road at the Muelle de Poniente and searched it
with support from the UPR prevention unit and the canine group. They found
the hashish and detained the driver, showing him the drugs found in the vehicle
he was driving.

The truck appeared empty and was heading toward boarding for Spain when a
specialist drugs dog alerted, prompting an exhaustive hours-long search inside
and outside the vehicle. After the hours-long detailed inspection, officers
found a large number of bags full of hashish inside the truck's structure.
Officers recovered numerous bags of hashish from the trailer's false bottom,
with first estimates putting the haul above 300 kilograms although police gave
no official weight. The submitted account describes the seizure as about
300 kilograms of hashish arriving from Morocco.

The handcuffed driver was taken to police headquarters and placed under
investigation for an offence against public health. A judge ordered the truck driver to be held in pre-trial detention on Sunday after he was brought before the court for an offence against public health. Police link the
operation to open UDYCO investigations into groups moving hashish from Ceuta to
mainland Spain in heavy vehicles with hidden compartments. The investigation remains open amid suspicion of larger loads and heavy vehicles hidden in storage places used as hashish stash houses.

report.summary: National Police arrested four men and one woman in Palma after intercepting a parcel with 24 kg of hashish and searching two homes where a further 36 kg was found. The second home also held 2 kg of cocaine and weapons, and police said the investigation remains open.
report.body:
National Police arrested four men and one woman in Palma on suspicion of
belonging to a group dedicated to drug trafficking. The Drug Group I of the
National Police ended an investigation started months before, with five
detained, police said. Officers learned of a parcel containing hashish
addressed to a man living in Palma. They identified him, seized the parcel
containing 24 kilos of hashish and detained him on suspicion of drug
trafficking. The investigation then led police to two homes where more
drugs might be held, and officers entered and searched the homes.

In the first home, the main suspect's dwelling, officers found 36 kilos of
hashish, an air rifle with a silencer and about 10,000 euros in cash.
Police detained the man and a woman there on suspicion of drug trafficking and
membership of a criminal group or organisation. In the second home police
detained a second suspect said to have kept and transported drugs. There
officers found 2 kilos of cocaine, several doses, cutting substance, a pistol
with 9-millimetre cartridges, a bow with arrows and a hydraulic press said to be
for compressing the cocaine.

A fifth person linked to the case was detained, and police said the drugs were
suspected to have been distributed to third parties for small-scale sale.
The investigation remains open and further arrests are not ruled out.
Officers from the Prevention and Reaction Unit, Drug Group II and the Canine
Guides also took part in the searches.

Police destroyed approximately 53,000 suspected cannabis plants after finding
two farms at Yaruni Bend, Linden, in the Upper Demerara River area, and the
farms covered about eight acres in total. The eradication exercise was
conducted by police ranks led by a Gazetted Officer between 5:30 a.m. and 4:36

and six feet in height, were found on two separate cannabis farms in the Upper

dried cannabis, camps and drying areas were destroyed by fire.

plants and the dried cannabis, at $22,038,728. No arrests were made, and
investigations are continuing.

Hong Kong Customs detected a drug-trafficking case involving baggage concealment
at Hong Kong International Airport on 5 November 2026. Customs seized about
9 kilograms of suspected cannabis buds with an estimated market value of about
$1.9 million. The 24-year-old mainland man had arrived from Bangkok,
Thailand, on the night of 4 November 2026.

In the early hours of 5 November, officers found the batch of buds in his
carry-on baggage during customs clearance. He was then arrested. He
was charged with one count of trafficking in a dangerous drug. The case was
to be brought before the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts on 6 November 2026.

Customs said it would continue to step up enforcement against drug trafficking
through intelligence analysis. Customs reminded the public not to accept
hiring or delegation from another party to carry controlled items into and out
of Hong Kong. Customs also reminded the public not to carry unknown items
for other people. Under the Dangerous Drugs Ordinance, trafficking in a
dangerous drug carries a maximum penalty of a $5 million fine and life
imprisonment on conviction.

report.body:
On October 8, 2026, Kern County Sheriff's Office deputies assigned to the Taft
substation, assisted by the Kern County Sheriff's Office High Intensity Drug
Trafficking Areas Task Force (KC-HIDTA) and the Taft Police Department, executed
a search warrant in the 27000 block of Hwy 119 in Taft. During the search
warrant, deputies eradicated a total of 660 marijuana plants at the cultivation
site in the 27000 block of Hwy 119 in Taft. Deputies additionally found
dangerous pesticides within the grow site in the 27000 block of Hwy 119 in Taft
during the search warrant operation.

Rogelio Lorenzo Francisca, 32, from Guerrero, Mexico, was arrested for HS
11358(c) cultivation of marijuana, HS 11359(b) marijuana for sale, PC 182(a)(1)
conspiracy and PC 148(a)(1) delay, resist or obstruct arrest and was booked into
the Taft jail facility. The investigation remained active and ongoing after
the October 8, 2026 Taft operation, with authorities saying they had not
released additional details about the operation. Anyone with information
about the case in Kern County was asked to contact the Kern County Sheriff's
Office at (661) 861-3110 or Kern Secret Witness at (661) 322-4040.

attempts.decision_title: South Africa cannabis legalisation is CFI history
attempts.explanation: The Al Jazeera piece is an explainer on South Africa's Cannabis for Private Purposes Act, signed by President Cyril Ramaphosa the day before the 27 May 2024 general elections, which removed cannabis from the list of outlawed narcotics and allowed adults to grow and consume it privately. It is a law change and reform history account, including the 2018 Constitutional Court ruling and a 2020 Haze Club raid mentioned only in passing. Under docs/CFI.md law changes, precedents and landmark cases belong to the Cannabis Freedom Index history, not to tracker enforcement-event reports, so no tracker draft is created. A suitable CFI-history source would be the Act itself or the Constitutional Court judgment.
